sources.entry: Webtor - Web-based torrent client with instant audio/video streaming. (Demo) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Webtor Self-Hosted is an all-in-one Docker image that runs the Webtor web-based torrent client, letting you stream or download files from torrents through a browser.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a self-hosted version of webtor.io as a single Docker container with an embedded PostgreSQL database and an embedded S3-compatible store. You can download individual files from a torrent directly, or stream video and audio files from a torrent immediately without downloading them fully first. Entire torrents can be downloaded as a ZIP archive built on the fly, preserving directory structure. A personal library organizes torrents, with movies and series detected automatically, and a Vault option saves torrent content permanently into the built-in store. The README also describes OpenSubtitles lookups, AI subtitle translation, AI-assisted enrichment and recommendations, a Stremio addon, and an embeddable player SDK for websites.
use_cases: stream a torrent video in the browser without waiting for download
download a single file from a torrent via direct link
download a whole torrent as a ZIP archive
watch torrent media on a TV via Stremio
embed a torrent video player on my own website
keep a personal library of movies and series from torrents
how_to_run: docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -v data:/data -v pgdata:/pgdata -v storage:/storage --name webtor --restart=always ghcr.io/webtor-io/self-hosted:latest
Open the web UI on the mapped port (8080 by default).
Optionally set ADMIN_PASSWORD to require login.
Optionally set DOMAIN to the address you use, or use an https reverse proxy for embedding on other sites.
notable: Instant audio and video streaming from torrents without full download
Vault saves torrent content permanently into the built-in S3 store
Optional AI subtitle translation and AI-assisted title recognition, each needing its own API key and switch
Embed-domain allow list controls which third-party sites can show the player
caveats: /storage must be a named Docker volume, not a bind mount, on macOS, Windows and some network filesystems
Embedding on other sites requires an https instance, and an https DOMAIN behind a reverse proxy
Several features (OpenSubtitles, metadata enrichment, AI features, SMTP email) need external API keys or servers and are off by default
keywords: watch movies from torrent in browser
